newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ports praise Clinton transport funding bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ports praise Clinton transport funding bill.

text.p: U.S. maritime ports on Friday hailed the Clinton administration's plan to spend $174 billion on transportation over the next six years, praising proposed funding increases for freight mobility and seaport development.

The administration's proposal, announced earlier this week, would reauthorize the sweeping Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act of 1991 (ISTEA) and raise current ISTEA funding levels by 11 percent. ISTEA is due to expire on September 30.

"The administration's proposal contains...some key provisions that will promote freight mobilitiy and projects providing improved access to America's seaports," Kurt Nagle, president of the American Association of Port Authorities, said in a statement.

"After hearing...over the past several years that ISTEA has not worked as well as it should to meet the needs of ports and freight mobility, the Department of Transportation has responded with specific ideas to improve the transportation planning process in those areas," he added.

AAPA praised several aspects of the proposed bill, called the National Economic Crossroads Transportation Efficiency Act, or NEXTEA, including enhanced port and rail connections to the National Highway System, and the expansion of the State Infrastructure Bank program.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
